item.title: DNA on cigarette leads to conviction in California cold case murder
item.description: A Sonoma County jury found 66-year-old James Oliver Unick guilty of the May 1982 murder.

item.title: Early voting underway in Arkansas for the March 3 primary & election
item.description: Arkansans can early vote from Feb. 17 through March 2 for the March 3 election, which includes a preferential primary and a special election for House District 70 and Senate District 26.

item.title: Arkansans remember Jesse Jackson and the impact he had locally
item.description: When news broke about Jesse Jackson's passing away at the age of 84, multiple organizations in Arkansas were remembering all the times he came to visit the Natural State. One of those organizations was the Mosaic Templars Cultural Center, who reminisced on one of the last times Jackson came to Little Rock in 2022.

item.title: AST Blog: 5 Years Since the February 2021 Deep Freeze
item.description: On February 14–15, snow and sleet spread across the state, and some spots saw snow coming down at rates up to 2 inches per hour. Little Rock ended that first round with 8.4 inches, and the cold was already intense, with high temperatures stuck in the single digits and teens across much of the state.

item.title: Discussing inaugural Black History Month panel with educator Nicole Griffin | Terrell Talk
item.description: This week, Donna chats with educator Nicole Griffin about an upcoming Black History Month panel featuring community members from across central Arkansas and beyond. Terrell Talk airs Tuesday nights at 7 p.m. along with live newscasts and other exclusive streaming content on the KARKFOX16+ app.

item.title: Central Arkansas potholes bring spike in tire damage, repairs
item.description: A recent surge in potholes across central Arkansas is sending more drivers to repair shops with damaged tires and wheels, while state transportation officials work to patch problem areas in the highway system and warn that the worst of pothole season may still be ahead.

item.title: ShotSpotter technology to stay after Little Rock city board approves renewal
item.description: Tuesday night, Little Rock city leaders voted to approve the renewal of a contract that will continue to keep ShotSpotter technology in the city.

item.title: Jefferson County Prosecuting Attorney says use of deadly force by Pine Bluff police in November 2025 shooting justified
item.description: The Jefferson County Prosecuting Attorney’s office has determined that the use of force by Pine Bluff Police Department officers after a pursuit last year was justified.

item.title: Taking a look at the past and future of Hall High School in Little Rock
item.description: The glory days of Hall High are still talked about and remembered by those who walked its halls, but its future is at stake.

item.title: University of Arkansas at Little Rock student receives national recognition for artwork
item.description: Every year, a jury with the Trump Kennedy Center selects 15 young artists with a disability to have their work displayed as a part of the Access/VSA Young Emerging Artists program. This year, one of Little Rock's own was selected for this honor.
